liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mr Charlie** (2 reviews): Mr. Charlie is called pretty rough, with Pigpen apparently off his game; Mr. Charlie is singled out as funky, and it hooked this listener [8][16]
- **Casey Jones** (2 reviews): Bob's guitar, prominent in the mix, has strong impact on Casey Jones; The reviewer says they enjoy Phil's playing in US Blues [13][16]
- **Smokestack Lightning** (1 review): Smokestack versions running ten to fifteen minutes could fill a whole concert by themselves [8]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Uncle John's Band is described as wonderful [10]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight is spectacular and extended; the show really takes off here [10]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Brokedown Palace is called the best ever by this listener [12]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bob's guitar, prominent in the mix, has strong impact on Bertha [13]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Phil's bass sounds rich and fat on Tennessee Jed [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd71-12-02 s1 t01 Intros**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd71-12-02 s1 t02 Bertha**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd71-12-02 s1 t03 Equipment Difficulties**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd71-12-02 s1 t04. Playin' In The Band**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd71-12-02 s1 t05 Mr. Charlie**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd71-12-02 s1 t06 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd71-12-02 s1 t07 Beat It On Down The Line**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd71-12-02 s1 t08 Black Peter**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-12-02.141424.fm.smith.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): FM broadcast; 32 songs; 175 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd71-12-02.sbd.lai.6255.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 161 min; rated 4.39/5 by 23 [6]. Said about its sound: Judged a better recording than the Felt Forum run days later; guitar sits higher and kick pedal lacks mechanical noise; Good sound overall, with a few minor glitches here and there; Excellent sound for 1971; Keith's piano fills out the sound, and Bob's guitar is high in the mix [8][9][13][14][18]
- **gd1971-12-02.142969.fm.smith.miller.clugston.pc.flac2496**: FM broadcast; 31 songs; 171 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1971-12-02.142968.fm.smith.miller.clugston.pc.flac1648**: FM broadcast; 31 songs; 171 min [3]

## Around the show

- The announcer's introduction reminded this listener of Mick Jagger [12]
- A mint-condition Felt Forum recording sounds better than this one, which has some technical problems [10]
- Fall 1971 is claimed to have the best versions of the new songs, better than Europe '72 [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-12-02.141424.fm.smith.miller.clugston.flac1644**: transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Matt Smith; source: Source Info: FM Broadcast (WBCN Boston); Master Reel to Reel > Matt Smith's 1st generation Reels; Transfer Info: 1st generation reels ((Technics RS-1506) >… [1].
